message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| # | Title | Year | Why it’s worth watching |
|---|-------|------|--------------------------|
| 1 | **The Shining** | 1980 | A masterclass in psychological dread, with iconic imagery and a chilling performance by Jack Nicholson. |
| 2 | **Hereditary** | 2018 | A deeply unsettling family drama that escalates into supernatural terror, featuring Toni Collette’s powerhouse acting. |
| 3 | **Get Out** | 2017 | A smart, socially conscious horror that blends satire with genuine scares, directed by Jordan Peele. |
| 4 | **The Babadook** | 2014 | A psychological horror about grief and motherhood, with a haunting creature that’s more metaphor than monster. |
| 5 | **A Quiet Place** | 2018 | Suspenseful, low‑budget filmmaking that relies on sound (or the lack of it) to build tension. |
| 6 | **It Follows** | 2014 | A fresh take on the “invisible threat” trope, with a creepy, relentless stalker that’s both simple and terrifying. |
| 7 | **Midsommar** | 2019 | A daylight horror that turns a Swedish festival into a nightmare, exploring cult rituals and psychological breakdown. |
| 8 | **The Conjuring** | 2013 | A well‑crafted supernatural thriller based on real‑life paranormal investigators Ed & Lorraine Warren. |
| 9 | **The Ring** | 2002 | A modern retelling of a Japanese horror classic, featuring a cursed videotape that brings death to anyone who watches it. |
|10 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | 2012 | A meta‑horror that subverts genre expectations while delivering plenty of gore and clever twists. |

Feel free to pick any that match your mood—whether you’re after psychological dread, supernatural chills, or a fresh twist on classic tropes!
